verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 52.2
verses.english: Linked Discourses 52.2

verses.pali: 1. Rahogatavagga
verses.english: 1. In Private

verses.pali: Dutiyarahogatasutta
verses.english: In Private (2nd)

verses.pali: Sāvatthinidānaṁ.
verses.english: At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmato anuruddhassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
verses.english: Then as Anuruddha was in private retreat this thought came to his mind:

verses.pali: “yesaṁ kesañci cattāro satipaṭṭhānā viraddhā, viraddho tesaṁ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī;
verses.english: “Whoever has missed out on these four kinds of mindfulness meditation has missed out on the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.

verses.pali: yesaṁ kesañci cattāro satipaṭṭhānā āraddhā, āraddho tesaṁ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī”ti.
verses.english: Whoever has undertaken these four kinds of mindfulness meditation has undertaken the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno āyasmato anuruddhassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—āyasmato anuruddhassa sammukhe pāturahosi. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno āyasmantaṁ anuruddhaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna knew what Venerable Anuruddha was thinking. As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he reappeared in front of Anuruddha and said to him:

verses.pali: “kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso anuruddha, bhikkhuno cattāro satipaṭṭhānā āraddhā hontī”ti?
verses.english: “Reverend Anuruddha, how do you define the undertaking of the four kinds of mindfulness meditation by a mendicant?”

verses.pali: “Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ajjhattaṁ kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: “Reverend, it’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body internally—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Bahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati …pe…
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of the body externally …

verses.pali: ajjhattabahiddhā kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: internally and externally—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings internally …

verses.pali: Bahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: externally …

verses.pali: Ajjhattabahiddhā vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: internally and externally …

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ citte …pe…
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of the mind internally …

verses.pali: bahiddhā citte …pe…
verses.english: externally …

verses.pali: ajjhattabahiddhā citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: internally and externally …

verses.pali: Ajjhattaṁ dhammesu …pe…
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of principles internally …

verses.pali: bahiddhā dhammesu …pe…
verses.english: externally …

verses.pali: ajjhattabahiddhā dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: internally and externally—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno cattāro satipaṭṭhānā āraddhā hontī”ti.
verses.english: That’s how to define the undertaking of the four kinds of mindfulness meditation by a mendicant.”

verses.pali: Dutiyaṁ.
